  Return value consists only of characters in `~r/\\A[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\\z/`.
  Encoding the same map twice produces identical output.

  def encode(%{feed: feed, direction: direction, keyset: keyset})
      when feed in [:feed, :public_feed, :hot_feed, :heat_feed, :author_feed] and
             direction in [:next, :prev] and is_binary(keyset) do
    data = serialize(feed, direction, keyset)
    sig = :crypto.mac(@mac, @hash, @secret, data)
    Base.url_encode64(data <> sig, padding: false)

  else (tampered, malformed, or hand-assembled payloads that never went through
  `encode/1`). Never raises.

    with {:ok, raw} <- Base.url_decode64(cursor, padding: false),
         {:len, len} when len > @sig_len <- {:len, byte_size(raw)},
         data = binary_part(raw, 0, len - @sig_len),
         sig = binary_part(raw, len - @sig_len, @sig_len),
         true <- secure_match?(sig, :crypto.mac(@mac, @hash, @secret, data)),
         {:term, term} <- deserialize(data),
         {:ok, payload} <- validate(term) do

  Supports :cursor-based continuation, limit/offset handling, and mapping of page
  results into a predictable response structure (`{items, next_cursor, prev_cursor, total}`).
  """

  @doc """
  Returns a single page of activities for `feed_name`.

  `opts` supports `:limit` (page size), `:cursor` (a value returned by `next_cursor`
  or `prev_cursor` from a previous call), and `:author_id` (required when
  `feed_name` is `:author_feed`).

  Returns `{:ok, %{items, next_cursor, prev_cursor, total, has_next, has_prev}}`
  on success, and `{:error, reason}` otherwise.

    with {:ok, config} <- fetch_config(feed_name),
         {action, default_limit, max_page_size} = config,
         {:ok, author_id} <- fetch_author_id(action, opts),
         {:ok, limit} <- fetch_limit(opts, default_limit, max_page_size),
         {:ok, cursor} <- decode_cursor(opts) do
      {:ok, cursor} = validate_cursor(cursor, feed_name)

      # Build the keyset/offset parameters for Ash. When no cursor was given
      # (null cursor) or its direction is forward, `after` sets the start point
      # and `before` is nil; when backward, `before` sets the start point and
      # `after` is nil.
      Ash.Query.new(Feed.Timeline.Activity)
      |> maybe_filter_author(author_id)
      |> Feed.Timeline.read(
        action: action,
        limit: limit,
        load: [:author, :reaction_count, :heat],
        after: cursor && cursor.direction == :next && cursor.keyset,
        before: cursor && cursor.direction == :prev && cursor.keyset
      )
      |> then(&build_result(&1, action, limit, author_id, cursor))
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Drives infinite scroll forward, starting at the first page and following
  `:next_cursor` until there is none.

  Returns `{:ok, %{pages: [activity_id_list], total: integer()}}`.
  """

    case fetch(feed_name, opts) do
      {:ok, page} ->
        {pages, total} = walk_forward(feed_name, opts, [page], page)

      error ->
        error

    public_feed: {:public_feed, 4, 25},
    hot_feed: {:hot_feed, 3, 25},
